evidence.claim: Cardholder C11923 disputes transaction 3583368 for $131.30 dated 2016-12-29 03:27:44.
Flagged amount $131.30 is 3.33x the 180-day mean of $39.45 (z=2.55) but below the card's observed max of $486.52, so it is unusual but not unprecedented.

Device 'SM-G610F Build/NRD90M | unknown | chrome 66.0 for android | unknown' is New for the account, but the card's baseline already spans 1,476 distinct devices over 10,286 online transactions, so a previously unseen device is routine for this card.
Channel and product are unchanged: 100% of the card's 10,286 baseline transactions are online product C, and the flagged transaction is online product C with no new region.

Two prior transactions on this card carry the identical $131.30 amount (3193355 in 2016-08, 3565743 in 2016-12), 123 days apart; looks_monthly is false, so R7's monthly recurring test is not met but a repeat merchant charge is plausible.

The flagged device profile appears on only 4 cards all-time (3 in window) and does not appear in the device lists of any of the high-fraud linked cards; the cards linked to this one share only ubiquitous strings such as 'Windows | unknown | chrome 66.0 | unknown', so no shared-origin ring is established.

The flagged card-testing run (3578451, 3578491, 3578496 then 3578506) did not clear a purchase over $100 and sits inside a stream of ~100 online transactions in the window, so it is background noise on a very high-volume card rather than a testing sequence tied to 3583368.

Semantic memory contains several cleared cases where a high-scoring purchase from a newly seen phone was confirmed by the cardholder (CC-3465, CC-0413), cautioning against treating the New device flag as proof.
Policy R2: on a customer denial, block the card and create a case; exposure of $131.30 is below the $1,000 reporting threshold and no credible shared-device link exists, so no regulatory report.
Customer maintained the denial and did not recognise the Samsung SM-G610F device when the earlier identical charges were put to them.

case.summary: C11923 disputes a single $131.30 online purchase (3583368) on card C11923-K2 made from a Samsung SM-G610F not previously seen on the account. The amount is 3.3x the card's mean but well inside its historical range, the channel and product match 100% of baseline activity, and the card already shows 1,476 distinct devices in 180 days, so the New-device flag is weak here. Two earlier charges for exactly $131.30 (3193355, 3565743) suggested a forgotten repeat merchant charge, so the cardholder was asked to reconcile them; they confirmed the older charges but maintained they placed no December order and do not know the device. On that denial the case moves to fraud under R2: block the card and open a case, with exposure limited to the single $131.30 transaction and no report warranted (under $1,000, no credible shared-device or ring link).

evidence_requests.assumed_response: Customer re-confirms they did not make the $131.30 purchase on 2016-12-29 and does not recognise the Samsung SM-G610F Android device; they say the earlier identical charges were their own repeat order with that merchant but they placed no order in December.

sar.reason: Case only, no report: fraud with exposure $131.30 <= $1,000, no shared device/region link and a documented pattern, so no §3a condition holds.

stop_reason: The verification response settled the repeat-charge question; exposure is only $131.30, below the R8 escalation and R2/s3a reporting thresholds, and no further graph evidence would change the block-and-case decision.
